target_customer: Consumers ordering restaurant food for delivery through apps
problem: Delivery demand was growing but restaurants were costly to run; Hideout ran a portfolio of delivery-only virtual restaurant brands out of shared kitchens.
business_model: operator of delivery-only restaurant brands, revenue from food sales on delivery apps

founders.name: Brian Leung
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio.

founders.name: Danielle Sobel
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; an unclaimed EmployBL profile credits her with founding the company in Los Angeles.

exit.reason: Cause not public; the YC directory marks the company Inactive.

competitors.name: Kitchen United
competitors.what: Delivery-focused shared kitchens, first site opened in Pasadena in 2018
competitors.traction_then: Hosted brands such as Dog Haus virtual kitchens in 2020

competitors.name: CloudKitchens
competitors.what: Ghost kitchen facilities started by Travis Kalanick, first facility in Los Angeles
competitors.traction_then: Dog Haus opened Innovation Kitchens with it in 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Menus, branding and delivery app listings; the difficulty was operational (kitchen partners, food quality, marketing), not technical.

defensibility.rationale: Virtual brands were easy for restaurants and rivals such as Virtual Dining Concepts to copy, and no proprietary supply or data is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later reporting says the ghost kitchen sector contracted after the pandemic, with Kitchen United pulling back and Wendy's closing its ghost kitchen business; no source mentions Hideout in that.

market_need_then: Delivery demand surged in 2020 and many operators launched virtual brands; no Hideout specific demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: Used findhideout.com, a prefixed domain, which redirected to a www host.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is generic and many unrelated restaurants share it; no press about the brand or community was found.

outcome_analysis: Hideout ran delivery-only restaurant brands from Los Angeles and went through Winter 2020 with a very small team. A single directory profile reports a pre-seed with no amount, and no shutdown report or post-mortem names the company, so the cause of going inactive is not public and failure factors are left empty. General coverage shows ghost kitchens fell out of favor after the pandemic, but no source ties that to Hideout.
notes: The pre-seed round rests on a single unclaimed EmployBL profile with hidden investors, amount and date; EmployBL also lists headcount 4 against the YC page's 1. The company site findhideout.com redirected with a 301 and was not followed further. Competitor source is a June 2020 trade article, a few months after the Winter 2020 batch; it names Kitchen United and CloudKitchens working with Dog Haus. Cause of inactivity not public.
